title: Polynomial Interpolation
description: Lagrange and Newton form, divided differences, Neville's scheme, error formula, Runge's phenomenon, Chebyshev nodes.
html:
📈 Polynomial Interpolation

1. Problem and Existence

For $n+1$ points $(x_i, y_i)$ with distinct nodes there is exactly one polynomial $p$ of degree $\le n$ with $p(x_i) = y_i$ (uniqueness: $p - q$ would have $n+1$ roots).

Monomial basis/Vandermonde matrix: correct but ill-conditioned.

2. Lagrange Form

$$p(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} y_i L_i(x), \qquad L_i(x) = \prod_{j \ne i}\frac{x - x_j}{x_i - x_j}, \quad \sum_i L_i = 1$$

3. Newton Form and Divided Differences

$$p(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} f[x_0..x_k]\prod_{j

Example

$(0,1), (1,3), (2,2)$: $f[0,1] = 2$, $f[1,2] = -1$, $f[0,1,2] = -1.5$ ⇒ $p(x) = 1 + 2x - 1.5\,x(x-1)$.

New point = one new term. Neville–Aitken: value at one point without the polynomial. Hermite: double node ⇒ derivative.

4. Error, Runge, Chebyshev

$$f(x) - p(x) = \frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi)}{(n+1)!}\prod_{i=0}^{n}(x - x_i)$$

  • Runge phenomenon: $\frac{1}{1+25x^2}$ with equidistant nodes – the error grows with $n$ (edges).
  • Chebyshev nodes $x_k = \cos\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{2n+2}$: $\max|\prod(x - x_k)| = 2^{-n}$ is minimal.
  • Extrapolation outside the nodes is risky.

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Wrong nodes in the product terms of the Newton form (they are $x_0, x_1, \dots$).
  • Confusing the degree with the number of points ($n+1$ points ⇒ degree $\le n$).
  • Choosing a high degree with equidistant nodes – prefer splines (4.10).
